subsystems.name: Robot units
subsystems.role: small, cheap mobile robots that physically assemble the structure.

subsystems.name: Swarm coordination
subsystems.role: lets many robots build without a central controller, using local rules and stigmergy.
parts: shared digital map or stigmergic markers

subsystems.name: Building blocks
subsystems.role: standardized components that robots can lift, place and connect.

subsystems.name: Localization and navigation
subsystems.role: each robot must know where it is and where to place the next block.

subsystems.name: Power and recharging
subsystems.role: keeps robots running for long build campaigns.

subsystems.name: Mission planning and oversight
subsystems.role: turns a human design into tasks for the swarm and monitors progress.

buildSteps.title: Design the robot unit
buildSteps.detail: Choose a simple, low-cost design: a small chassis, a gripper, basic sensors and a radio. The goal is many cheap robots rather than a few complex ones.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture the units
buildSteps.detail: Mass-produce chassis, motors, electronics and grippers, then assemble and test each robot for reliability.

buildSteps.title: Develop swarm algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Write local rules that let robots coordinate through the environment (stigmergy) or short-range radio. Test extensively in simulation before hardware.

buildSteps.title: Design the building blocks
buildSteps.detail: Create standard blocks or modules that are easy to grasp, align and lock together, with features that help robots sense correct placement.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the site
buildSteps.detail: Level the ground, deploy localization beacons or markers, and set up charging stations and material depots.

buildSteps.title: Compile the build plan
buildSteps.detail: Convert a human CAD design into a sequence of swarm rules and waypoints, so robots know what to build without central instruction.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and build
buildSteps.detail: Release the robots onto the site. They work in parallel, sensing local progress and adding blocks until the structure is complete.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and adapt
buildSteps.detail: Humans watch a dashboard and step in only for errors or recharging. Robots detect and correct mistakes using local checks.

prerequisites.why: demonstrated in lab settings with tens of robots, but scaling to thousands with robust coordination is unsolved.
small motors and grippers are widely available, though they must be cheap enough for disposable robots.
accurate indoor localization works, but reliable, low-power communication for thousands of robots on an open construction site is not yet proven.
robots can stack blocks in labs, but handling heavy or precision components for infrastructure is beyond current demos.
batteries and recharging exist, but keeping thousands of robots running for weeks without human intervention is difficult.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations of tens of robots building simple towers or walls using stigmergy
pathway.unlocks: proof that decentralized coordination can produce ordered structures.

pathway.milestone: field trials with hundreds of robots building small-scale structures like shelters or modular walls
pathway.unlocks: reliability data and better algorithms for real-world noise.

pathway.milestone: pilot projects for specific infrastructure tasks, such as assembling modular bridges or laying blocks in hazardous areas
pathway.unlocks: commercial niches where human access is dangerous or expensive.

pathway.milestone: thousands of robots building large infrastructure autonomously with minimal human oversight
pathway.unlocks: rapid, low-cost construction in remote or extreme environments.
